evidence: 0fed8d43398d formal 36/36, geo_mean 0.710539x; small inputs (1K-1M elems) 20.5-21.2us vs reference 13.5-13.9us. host-profile-fast: uninstrumented submit 19.60us; 1000 hit calls still traverse run -> _selu_inplace -> _select_block -> _launch_cached_flat -> _debug_forced_fallback -> _current_device_index -> _do_launch; _launch_cached_flat self 4.56us, _debug_forced_fallback 1.90us, _current_device_index 1.00us, _select_block 1.78us, 8000 getattr 1.39us, bound launcher.launch (C) 12.39us.
mechanism: Cache-hit path redundantly recomputes dtype-derived block/mask, re-walks cold-path helper layers, and re-reads fixed compile metadata (compile_only/msprof/debug flags and launcher metadata) on every launch. Those properties are constant for the lifetime of one compiled artifact; only dynamic state (input pointer, current stream, current device) needs re-reading. Removing the fixed part from the per-call path cuts Python-side launch latency that dominates small-input timing.
change: Add _FAST_CACHE keyed by (device_index, dtype, numel) holding bound launch, function, packed_metadata, integer grid, masked flag and n. Fill it in _launch_cached_flat only after the debug/compile-only/msprof checks pass and the single ABI launch succeeds; debug/profiling artifacts never enter it. run() performs the hit path inline: contiguity, dtype/numel/device key, 16B pointer alignment, current device via a module-init-cached _npu_getDevice function object (public current_device fallback), current raw stream via the existing NoWait-first query, then one direct ABI launch. Miss/unaligned/non-contiguous/device-mismatch fall back to the original _selu_inplace path; kernels, block selection and numerics are unchanged. Exceptions after emission are not retried.
prediction: Small-input host submit drops from ~19.6us by roughly the removed Python overhead (a few us); large-input timings (~45.5/83.2/87.2us) stay unchanged. Small-case candidate time should move toward the reference side; formal geo_mean should rise above 0.710539x.
